name: MiniCPM5-2B-Jev
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B (config.json max_position_embeddings 131072). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: GQA, 16 query heads and 2 kv heads
notes: ADDED 2026-11-06. A finetune of openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B, not a new base model: same config.json, same 2.517 parameters (identical tensor set). Recorded as a contender because it publishes benchmark evidence against its own base; the evidence rows below are card-sourced and marked vendor_claim. Licence apache-2.0, repo created 2026-09-28. CAVEAT ON THE COMPARISON: this card scores a 231-decision JevBench suite (Easy 48 / Standard 72 / Hard 111); the catalog's jul-decision-minicpm5-2b records 68.0 on a 300-question jev-bench run of the same family, so the two numbers are NOT row-comparable and neither supersedes the other. Against the SAME table's own base row the delta is real: MiniCPM5-2B untuned 62.5% overall / 0.693 Brier / 0.272 ECE versus 78.8% / 0.214 / 0.031 here - all bf16, no quant in the base column. The card names no external harness beyond the suite (fstandhartinger/jevbench) and does not print latency; no per-tier base number is printed, only the overall base row. It is a LoRA adapter (library_name peft, base_model_relation adapter) - the repo root alone is not the decision model. Excluded from the worth-running ranking by task=decision, ranked in docs/33-decision-models.md.

benchmarks.name: JevBench overall (231 decisions)
benchmarks.config: Card table 'JevBench Public Decision Suite', column 'MiniCPM5-2B-Jev (Ours)', overall micro accuracy 78.79%. Base row on the SAME table is 'MiniCPM5-2B (Untuned Base, Step 0)' at 62.5% - a real bf16 base run, not a quant. Card also prints per-tier: Easy 97.9 vs 100.0 for Jev hosted, Standard 94.4, Hard 60.4. No harness name printed beyond the suite itself (fstandhartinger/jevbench); model-index YAML repeats 0.7879.

benchmarks.name: JevBench Standard/Original tier (72 items)
benchmarks.config: Same card table, 'Standard (72)' column: 94.4% vs 94.4 for decider-35b-a3b v1, 94.4 for SemIf; Jev hosted 98.6. Above decider-2b v11 88.9 and system-one 88.9.

benchmarks.name: JevBench Hard tier (111 items)
benchmarks.config: Same card table, 'Hard (111)' column: 60.4% vs 67.6 decider-35b-a3b v1, 64.9 decider-4b v2.1, 64.0 OpenJev, 57.7 decider-2b v11, 54.1 Kev-4B. LOSSES to every 4B+ decider above it.

benchmarks.name: JevBench calibration ECE
benchmarks.config: Card table 'Accuracy / Brier / ECE', ECE column (lower is better): 0.031 vs 0.056 Kev-4B as served, 0.088 Kev-0.8B, 0.272 untuned MiniCPM5-2B base. Second-lowest on the card after Kev-9B 0.042 is beaten - 0.031 is the best ECE printed. Brier 0.214 vs base 0.693.
